name: What should luxury homeowners in Los Angeles prioritize first: architecture, interiors, or construction?

mainEntity.name: In a luxury home project, what should come first: architecture, interior design, or construction?
mainEntity.text: In a luxury home project, what should come first: architecture, interior design, or construction?

acceptedAnswer.text: Luxury residential projects work best when architecture, interior design, and construction are treated as one coordinated process instead of separate steps. Architecture usually comes first because it establishes the structure, layout, and major building decisions. Interior design then translates those spaces into a livable, beautiful home by defining materials, lighting, finishes, and furnishings. Construction brings the vision to life, but it depends on clear planning from the other two disciplines. In Los Angeles, the projects that feel most seamless are usually the ones where the three teams collaborate early. If the architect designs a room without considering the furniture layout, or the builder starts before finish decisions are complete, the result can be expensive and awkward. Homeowners should look for a process that connects all three from the start so the finished house feels unified.
acceptedAnswer.description: Architecture should establish the structure and layout, interior design should define how the home feels and functions, and construction should execute the plan. The best results come when all three are coordinated early, because luxury homes depend on alignment between space planning, materials, and build quality.
